name: Alternator
summary: A small generator, driven by the engine, that charges the battery and powers the electrics while you drive.
whatItDoes: Once the engine is running, the alternator supplies the car's electricity and tops the battery back up.
howItWorks: The accessory belt spins the alternator's pulley. Inside, a spinning electromagnet (the rotor) turns within fixed copper windings (the stator) and makes alternating current. Diodes turn that into direct current, and a voltage regulator keeps the output at roughly 13.5 to 14.5 volts.
failureSymptoms: Whining or grinding from the alternator
toolsNeeded: Belt tensioner tool or long breaker bar
safetyNotes: Disconnect the battery first. The alternator's main output wire is live all the time.
Keep hands clear of the belt and fan. Never work on the belt with the engine running.
